**Apple Scab**

Apple scab is the most common disease of apple and crabapple trees in Minnesota.
Scab is caused by a fungus that infects both leaves and fruit.
Scabby fruit are often unfit for eating.
Infected leaves have olive green to brown spots.
Leaves with many leaf spots turn yellow and fall off early.
Leaf loss weakens the tree when it occurs many years in a row.
Planting disease resistant varieties is the best way to manage scab.

**Prevention and treatment:** Choose resistant varieties when possible.
Rake under trees and destroy infected leaves to reduce the number of fungal spores available to start the disease cycle over again next spring.
Water in the evening or early morning hours (avoid overhead irrigation) to give the leaves time to dry out before infection can occur.
Spread a 3- to 6-inch layer of compost under trees, keeping it away from the trunk, to cover soil and prevent splash dispersal of the fungal spores.
For best control, spray liquid copper soap early, two weeks before symptoms normally appear. Alternatively, begin applications when disease first appears, and repeat at 7 to 10 day intervals up to blossom drop. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

How to prevent Apple Cedar rust?

**Apple Cedar rust**

Cedar apple rust (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae) is a fungal disease that requires juniper plants to complete its complicated two year life-cycle. Spores overwinter as a reddish-brown gall on young twigs of various juniper species. In early spring, during wet weather, these galls swell and bright orange masses of spores are blown by the wind where they infect susceptible apple and crab-apple trees. The spores that develop on these trees will only infect junipers the following year. From year to year, the disease must pass from junipers to apples to junipers again; it cannot spread between apple trees.

**Prevention and treatment:** Choose resistant cultivars when available.
Rake up and dispose of fallen leaves and other debris from under trees.
Remove galls from infected junipers. In some cases, juniper plants should be removed entirely.
Apply preventative, disease-fighting fungicides labeled for use on apples weekly, starting with bud break, to protect trees from spores being released by the juniper host. This occurs only once per year, so additional applications after this springtime spread are not necessary.
On juniper, rust can be controlled by spraying plants with a copper solution (0.5 to 2.0 oz/ gallon of water) at least four times between late August and late October.
Safely treat most fungal and bacterial diseases with SERENADE Garden. This broad spectrum bio-fungicide uses a patented strain of Bacillus subtilis that is registered for organic use. What is Potato Early Blight and how do I treat it?

**Potato Early Blight**

In most production areas, early blight occurs annually to some degree. The severity of early blight is dependent upon the frequency of foliar wetness from rain, dew, or irrigation; the nutritional status of the foliage; and cultivar susceptibility.The first symptoms of early blight appear as small, circular or irregular, dark-brown to black spots on the older (lower) leaves. These spots enlarge up to 3/8 inch in diameter and gradually may become angular-shaped.Initial lesions on young, fully expanded leaves may be confused with brown spot lesions. These first lesions appear about two to three days after infection, with further sporulation on the surface of these lesions occurring three to five days later.

**Prevention and treatment:** Treatment of early blight includes prevention by planting potato varieties that are resistant to the disease; late maturing are more resistant than early maturing varieties. Avoid overhead irrigation and allow for sufficient aeration between plants to allow the foliage to dry as quickly as possible. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

What is the benefit of Soil Health Card Scheme?

**Soil Health Card Scheme** (Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare))

Launched in 2015, the scheme provides every farm holding with a printed Soil Health Card giving the current status of soil nutrients and crop-wise recommendations of fertiliser and soil amendments. Cards report 12 parameters - pH, electrical conductivity, organic carbon, available nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, sulphur, and the micronutrients zinc, boron, iron, manganese and copper. From 2022-23 the scheme is a component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) as 'Soil Health & Fertility'.

**Benefit:** Free soil testing and a free Soil Health Card that lets farmers cut wasteful fertiliser use - field studies show 8-10% reduction in chemical fertiliser use and 5-6% higher yield when recommendations are followed. Assistance is also given for setting up village-level soil testing labs (up to Rs 5 lakh for a static lab and support for mini/mobile labs) and for Model Villages where soil sampling is done on each holding.

**Eligibility:** All farmers with an agricultural land holding, irrespective of size or category, in every state and union territory. Rural youth and FPOs can apply for assistance to set up village-level soil testing laboratories under the entrepreneurship component.

**How to apply:** Contact the village agriculture extension officer, the Krishi Vigyan Kendra or the block/district agriculture office to have a soil sample drawn from your field, or submit a sample at a designated soil testing laboratory. Registration and card download are available at https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in and on the Soil Health Card mobile app; the card can be searched by Aadhaar, mobile number or the card's sample number.

Official site: https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in

For 0.5 acre of muskmelon (about 0.202 ha):
- Urea: 35.4 kg (~0.7 bags)
- DAP: 22.0 kg (~0.4 bags)
- MOP: 16.9 kg (~0.3 bags)

**Schedule:**
- Basal (at sowing/transplanting): full DAP, full MOP, 1/3 Urea
- First top dressing (3-4 weeks): 1/3 Urea
- Second top dressing (flowering/panicle initiation): 1/3 Urea

messages.name: crop_guide
messages.content: {"season": "Rabi crop, a hardy cereal grown in marginal and saline/alkaline soils.", "climate": "Cool dry climate, 12-25 C, more tolerant of drought, frost and salinity than wheat.", "soil": "Wide adaptability including light, saline/alkaline and marginal soils, pH up to 9.5 tolerated.", "sowing_time": "Mid-October to mid-November (timely sown).", "seed_rate": "100 kg/ha irrigated timely sown; 125 kg/ha late sown/rainfed.", "spacing": "Rows 20-22.5 cm apart.", "irrigation": "2-3 irrigations sufficient (more drought-hardy than wheat); critical at crown root initiation and jointing.", "fertilizer_schedule": "60-80:30-40:20 NPK kg/ha; half N and full P,K basal, remaining N at first irrigation (CRI stage).", "major_pests_diseases": "Aphid, termite; yellow rust, covered smut, foliar blights.", "harvest": "120-140 days; harvest at physiological maturity, March-April.", "expected_yield": "35-45 q/ha irrigated.", "improved_varieties": "DWRB 137, RD 2552, BH 393, Karan 16 (DWRB 91), Azad."}

**Barley cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Rabi crop, a hardy cereal grown in marginal and saline/alkaline soils.
- **Soil:** Wide adaptability including light, saline/alkaline and marginal soils, pH up to 9.5 tolerated.
- **Sowing Time:** Mid-October to mid-November (timely sown).
- **Seed Rate:** 100 kg/ha irrigated timely sown; 125 kg/ha late sown/rainfed.
- **Spacing:** Rows 20-22.5 cm apart.
- **Irrigation:** 2-3 irrigations sufficient (more drought-hardy than wheat); critical at crown root initiation and jointing.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 60-80:30-40:20 NPK kg/ha; half N and full P,K basal, remaining N at first irrigation (CRI stage).
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Aphid, termite; yellow rust, covered smut, foliar blights.
- **Harvest:** 120-140 days; harvest at physiological maturity, March-April.
- **Expected Yield:** 35-45 q/ha irrigated.
- **Improved Varieties:** DWRB 137, RD 2552, BH 393, Karan 16 (DWRB 91), Azad. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

messages.content: {"season": "Perennial plantation crop; planting done at monsoon onset.", "climate": "Tropical humid climate, 27-32 C, well-distributed rainfall 100-230 cm.", "soil": "Sandy loam to laterite coastal soils, well-drained, pH 5.2-8.0.", "sowing_time": "Planting of seedlings May-June (monsoon onset) or Sept-Oct.", "seed_rate": "About 175 seedlings/ha at standard spacing.", "spacing": "7.5 m x 7.5 m (square system) for tall varieties.", "irrigation": "40 litres/palm/week in summer if irrigated; drip irrigation with 20-30 litres/day improves yield.", "fertilizer_schedule": "500 g N, 320 g P2O5, 1200 g K2O per palm per year in two splits, with 25-50 kg organic manure/palm.", "major_pests_diseases": "Rhinoceros beetle, red palm weevil, eriophyid mite; bud rot, root wilt disease.", "harvest": "First bearing in 5-6 years; nuts mature 12 months after spathe opening, harvested every 45-60 days.", "expected_yield": "80-100 nuts/palm/year under good management.", "improved_varieties": "West Coast Tall, Chowghat Orange Dwarf, Kera Chandra (T x D hybrid)."}

**Coconut cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Perennial plantation crop; planting done at monsoon onset.
- **Soil:** Sandy loam to laterite coastal soils, well-drained, pH 5.2-8.0.
- **Sowing Time:** Planting of seedlings May-June (monsoon onset) or Sept-Oct.
- **Seed Rate:** About 175 seedlings/ha at standard spacing.
- **Spacing:** 7.5 m x 7.5 m (square system) for tall varieties.
- **Irrigation:** 40 litres/palm/week in summer if irrigated; drip irrigation with 20-30 litres/day improves yield.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 500 g N, 320 g P2O5, 1200 g K2O per palm per year in two splits, with 25-50 kg organic manure/palm.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Rhinoceros beetle, red palm weevil, eriophyid mite; bud rot, root wilt disease.
- **Harvest:** First bearing in 5-6 years; nuts mature 12 months after spathe opening, harvested every 45-60 days.
- **Expected Yield:** 80-100 nuts/palm/year under good management.
- **Improved Varieties:** West Coast Tall, Chowghat Orange Dwarf, Kera Chandra (T x D hybrid). Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

messages.name: crop_guide
messages.content: {"season": "Kharif (main) and Rabi/summer under irrigation in South India.", "climate": "Warm climate 25-30 C, sensitive to frost and waterlogging, needs 50-125 cm rainfall.", "soil": "Well-drained sandy loam, light in texture, pH 6.0-7.0; calcium availability important for pegging.", "sowing_time": "Kharif: June-July; Rabi/summer: Jan-Feb (irrigated, South India).", "seed_rate": "100-120 kg pods/ha; 80-100 kg kernels/ha of bold varieties.", "spacing": "30 cm x 10 cm for spreading types; 30 cm x 15 cm for bunch types.", "irrigation": "Rainfed in Kharif; summer/Rabi crop irrigated every 10-12 days, critical at pegging and pod development.", "fertilizer_schedule": "20:40:40 NPK kg/ha plus gypsum 400-500 kg/ha at flowering/pegging for pod filling.", "major_pests_diseases": "Leaf miner, thrips, white grub; tikka leaf spot (early and late), rust, collar rot.", "harvest": "100-130 days; harvest when leaves yellow and pods show netted veins/darker inner shell colour.", "expected_yield": "15-20 q/ha (pods) rainfed; 25-30 q/ha irrigated.", "improved_varieties": "TAG 24, GG 20, TG 37A, Girnar 4, Dharani (TCGS 1043)."}

**Groundnut cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Kharif (main) and Rabi/summer under irrigation in South India.
- **Soil:** Well-drained sandy loam, light in texture, pH 6.0-7.0; calcium availability important for pegging.
- **Sowing Time:** Kharif: June-July; Rabi/summer: Jan-Feb (irrigated, South India).
- **Seed Rate:** 100-120 kg pods/ha; 80-100 kg kernels/ha of bold varieties.
- **Spacing:** 30 cm x 10 cm for spreading types; 30 cm x 15 cm for bunch types.
- **Irrigation:** Rainfed in Kharif; summer/Rabi crop irrigated every 10-12 days, critical at pegging and pod development.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 20:40:40 NPK kg/ha plus gypsum 400-500 kg/ha at flowering/pegging for pod filling.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Leaf miner, thrips, white grub; tikka leaf spot (early and late), rust, collar rot.
- **Harvest:** 100-130 days; harvest when leaves yellow and pods show netted veins/darker inner shell colour.
- **Expected Yield:** 15-20 q/ha (pods) rainfed; 25-30 q/ha irrigated.
- **Improved Varieties:** TAG 24, GG 20, TG 37A, Girnar 4, Dharani (TCGS 1043). Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

**Kidneybeans cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Kharif crop in hills, Rabi crop in plains.
- **Soil:** Well-drained loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.0-7.5.
- **Sowing Time:** Hills (Kharif): April-May; plains (Rabi): Oct-Nov.
- **Seed Rate:** 80-100 kg/ha for bold-seeded rajma types.
- **Spacing:** 45 cm x 10 cm.
- **Irrigation:** 4-5 irrigations in plains; critical at flowering and pod formation; hill crop mostly rainfed.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 20:60:40 NPK kg/ha; full dose basal, light N top-dress at flowering if needed.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Aphid, pod borer, bean fly; anthracnose, angular leaf spot, bean common mosaic virus.
- **Harvest:** 90-120 days; harvest when pods dry and rattle.
- **Expected Yield:** 12-18 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** PDR 14, Uttara, VL Rajma 63, HUR 15, Arka Suvidha. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

**Lentil cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Rabi crop, mainly grown as a pulse in North and Central India.
- **Soil:** Well-drained sandy loam to clay loam, pH 6.0-7.5.
- **Sowing Time:** Mid-October to mid-November.
- **Seed Rate:** 30-40 kg/ha (bold seeded); 25-30 kg/ha (small seeded).
- **Spacing:** Row spacing 25-30 cm.
- **Irrigation:** Mostly grown on residual moisture; one irrigation at pre-flowering/pod-formation stage if available.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 20:40:20 NPK kg/ha, all basal at sowing; seed inoculation with Rhizobium recommended.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Aphid, pod borer; rust, wilt, Ascochyta blight.
- **Harvest:** 110-130 days; harvest when pods turn brown and dry, Feb-March.
- **Expected Yield:** 12-15 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** Pusa Vaibhav, DPL 62 (Asha), IPL 316, Pant Masur 639. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

messages.name: crop_guide
messages.content: {"season": "Perennial; flowering Dec-Feb, fruiting April-July.", "climate": "Tropical/subtropical; dry weather during flowering favours fruit set, sensitive to frost.", "soil": "Deep well-drained alluvial to laterite loam, pH 5.5-7.5.", "sowing_time": "Planting of grafted plants July-Aug (rainfed) or Feb-March (irrigated).", "seed_rate": "100-400 grafted plants/ha depending on spacing (traditional to high-density).", "spacing": "10 m x 10 m traditional; 5 m x 5 m for high-density planting.", "irrigation": "Irrigate at 10-15 day intervals during fruit development; withhold irrigation before flowering to induce stress-flowering.", "fertilizer_schedule": "1-1.5 kg N, 0.5 kg P2O5, 1 kg K2O per bearing tree per year, applied post-harvest and before flowering.", "major_pests_diseases": "Mango hopper, mealybug, fruit fly; powdery mildew, anthracnose, malformation.", "harvest": "Bearing starts 4-5 years after grafting; fruits mature 3-4.5 months after fruit set, April-July.", "expected_yield": "8-12 tonnes/ha at full bearing.", "improved_varieties": "Alphonso, Dashehari, Langra, Kesar, Amrapali, Mallika."}

**Mango cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Perennial; flowering Dec-Feb, fruiting April-July.
- **Soil:** Deep well-drained alluvial to laterite loam, pH 5.5-7.5.
- **Sowing Time:** Planting of grafted plants July-Aug (rainfed) or Feb-March (irrigated).
- **Seed Rate:** 100-400 grafted plants/ha depending on spacing (traditional to high-density).
- **Spacing:** 10 m x 10 m traditional; 5 m x 5 m for high-density planting.
- **Irrigation:** Irrigate at 10-15 day intervals during fruit development; withhold irrigation before flowering to induce stress-flowering.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 1-1.5 kg N, 0.5 kg P2O5, 1 kg K2O per bearing tree per year, applied post-harvest and before flowering.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Mango hopper, mealybug, fruit fly; powdery mildew, anthracnose, malformation.
- **Harvest:** Bearing starts 4-5 years after grafting; fruits mature 3-4.5 months after fruit set, April-July.
- **Expected Yield:** 8-12 tonnes/ha at full bearing.
- **Improved Varieties:** Alphonso, Dashehari, Langra, Kesar, Amrapali, Mallika. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

**Mothbeans cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Kharif crop, a hardy drought-tolerant pulse of arid regions.
- **Soil:** Sandy to sandy loam soils of low fertility, pH 6.0-8.0, tolerant of poor soils.
- **Sowing Time:** June-July with the onset of monsoon.
- **Seed Rate:** 8-10 kg/ha broadcast; 5-6 kg/ha line sowing.
- **Spacing:** 30-45 cm x 10-15 cm.
- **Irrigation:** Purely rainfed; extremely drought-tolerant, no irrigation normally needed.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 10-20:20-40:0 NPK kg/ha basal, reflecting low fertility requirement.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Aphid, pod borer, whitefly; yellow mosaic virus, bacterial leaf spot, powdery mildew.
- **Harvest:** 75-90 days; harvest when pods dry and turn brown.
- **Expected Yield:** 5-8 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** RMO 40, RMO 225, CAZRI Moth 2, Jadia. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

**Mungbean cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Grown in Kharif, summer (Zaid) and spring seasons depending on region.
- **Soil:** Well-drained sandy loam to loam, pH 6.5-7.5.
- **Sowing Time:** Kharif: June-July; summer/Zaid: March-April.
- **Seed Rate:** 15-20 kg/ha.
- **Spacing:** 30 cm x 10 cm.
- **Irrigation:** Rainfed in Kharif; summer crop needs 4-5 irrigations at 10-12 day intervals, critical at flowering and pod development.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 20:40:20 NPK kg/ha basal; seed treatment with Rhizobium culture.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Whitefly (yellow mosaic virus vector), thrips, pod borer; yellow mosaic virus, Cercospora leaf spot, powdery mildew.
- **Harvest:** 60-75 days; 2-3 pickings as pods mature and turn black.
- **Expected Yield:** 8-10 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** Pusa Vishal, SML 668, IPM 2-3 (Virat), Samrat, Pusa 1431. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

**Muskmelon cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Zaid (summer) crop; also grown as a riverbed crop.
- **Soil:** Sandy loam, well-drained, pH 6.5-7.5; sandy river-bed soils are ideal.
- **Sowing Time:** January-March (Zaid); Nov-Dec on riverbeds.
- **Seed Rate:** 3-4 kg/ha.
- **Spacing:** 2 m x 0.6 m on raised beds/pits.
- **Irrigation:** Irrigate every 5-7 days; critical at flowering and fruit development, avoid water stress.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 100:50:50 NPK kg/ha; half N and full P, K basal, remaining N at vine spread and flowering.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Fruit fly, red pumpkin beetle, aphid; powdery mildew, downy mildew, fusarium wilt.
- **Harvest:** 80-100 days after sowing; harvest at full slip/aroma stage.
- **Expected Yield:** 15-20 tonnes/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** Punjab Sunehri, Pusa Sharbati, Hara Madhu, Arka Jeet. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

**Onion cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Rabi (main, Nov-Dec transplant), also Kharif and late Kharif in different zones.
- **Soil:** Well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.0-7.5.
- **Sowing Time:** Nursery: Oct-Nov (Rabi); transplanting 5-6 weeks later in December.
- **Seed Rate:** 8-10 kg/ha for nursery raising.
- **Spacing:** 15 cm x 10 cm.
- **Irrigation:** Irrigate every 7-10 days; stop irrigation 2-3 weeks before harvest for better curing and storage.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 100:50:50 NPK kg/ha; half N and full P,K basal, remaining N in two splits at 30 and 45 DAT.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Thrips, onion maggot; purple blotch, Stemphylium blight, basal rot.
- **Harvest:** 110-150 days after transplanting; harvest when 50-75% tops fall over and neck softens.
- **Expected Yield:** 250-350 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** Pusa Red, Agrifound Dark Red, Bhima Super, N-53, Pusa Riddhi. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

**Orange cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Perennial; two flowering flushes - Ambia (Jan-Feb) and Mrig (June-July).
- **Soil:** Deep well-drained loam, pH 5.5-7.5; avoid waterlogged/saline soils.
- **Sowing Time:** Planting of grafted saplings June-Aug or Feb-March.
- **Seed Rate:** 275-400 grafted plants/ha depending on spacing.
- **Spacing:** 6 m x 6 m.
- **Irrigation:** Drip irrigation preferred, 15-20 irrigations/year; a stress period before Mrig bahar improves flowering.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 600-800 g N, 200-300 g P2O5, 200-300 g K2O per bearing tree per year, split in 2-3 doses.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Citrus psylla, leaf miner, fruit-sucking moth; citrus canker, gummosis, greening (Huanglongbing).
- **Harvest:** First bearing in 4-5 years; fruits mature 8-10 months after flowering, Nov-Jan for Nagpur mandarin.
- **Expected Yield:** 15-20 tonnes/ha at full bearing.
- **Improved Varieties:** Nagpur Mandarin, Kinnow, Coorg Mandarin, Mosambi (sweet orange). Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

messages.content: {"season": "Grown year-round; best planting Feb-March and June-July.", "climate": "Tropical/subtropical, frost-free, 22-32 C optimum.", "soil": "Well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.0-7.0; sensitive to waterlogging.", "sowing_time": "Nursery raising in poly bags, transplanting Feb-March or Sept-Oct.", "seed_rate": "300-400 g seed/ha for raising about 2000 plants/ha.", "spacing": "1.8-2.0 m x 1.8-2.0 m.", "irrigation": "Drip irrigation preferred; irrigate every 3-4 days in summer, avoid waterlogging.", "fertilizer_schedule": "250:250:500 g NPK/plant/year in monthly split doses with 10 kg FYM/plant.", "major_pests_diseases": "Papaya mealybug, fruit fly, aphid (virus vector); papaya ring spot virus, powdery mildew, foot rot.", "harvest": "First harvest 9-11 months after planting; fruits picked at colour-break stage.", "expected_yield": "60-80 tonnes/ha/year.", "improved_varieties": "Pusa Delicious, Red Lady 786, Taiwan 786, CO 7, Pusa Nanha."}

**Papaya cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Grown year-round; best planting Feb-March and June-July.
- **Soil:** Well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.0-7.0; sensitive to waterlogging.
- **Sowing Time:** Nursery raising in poly bags, transplanting Feb-March or Sept-Oct.
- **Seed Rate:** 300-400 g seed/ha for raising about 2000 plants/ha.
- **Spacing:** 1.8-2.0 m x 1.8-2.0 m.
- **Irrigation:** Drip irrigation preferred; irrigate every 3-4 days in summer, avoid waterlogging.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 250:250:500 g NPK/plant/year in monthly split doses with 10 kg FYM/plant.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Papaya mealybug, fruit fly, aphid (virus vector); papaya ring spot virus, powdery mildew, foot rot.
- **Harvest:** First harvest 9-11 months after planting; fruits picked at colour-break stage.
- **Expected Yield:** 60-80 tonnes/ha/year.
- **Improved Varieties:** Pusa Delicious, Red Lady 786, Taiwan 786, CO 7, Pusa Nanha. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

**Pigeonpeas cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Kharif crop, long duration (150-270 days).
- **Soil:** Deep well-drained loam to clay loam, pH 6.5-7.5.
- **Sowing Time:** June-July with monsoon onset.
- **Seed Rate:** 15-20 kg/ha sole crop; 8-10 kg/ha as intercrop.
- **Spacing:** 60-75 cm x 20-30 cm for short-duration types; 90-120 cm x 30 cm for long-duration types.
- **Irrigation:** Mostly rainfed; 1-2 protective irrigations at flowering and pod filling if available.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 20-25:50:20 NPK kg/ha basal; Rhizobium seed treatment recommended.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Pod borer (Helicoverpa), pod fly; Fusarium wilt, sterility mosaic disease.
- **Harvest:** 150-180 days for medium-duration types; harvest when 80% pods dry, Dec-Feb.
- **Expected Yield:** 12-18 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** Pusa 2001, ICPL 87119 (Asha), UPAS 120, Manak, BSMR 736. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

**Pomegranate cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Perennial; flowered as Ambe (Jan-Feb), Mrig (June-July) or Hasta (Sept-Oct) bahar.
- **Soil:** Deep loamy to medium black soil, well-drained, pH 6.5-7.5; tolerant of moderate salinity.
- **Sowing Time:** Planting of rooted cuttings/grafts June-July or Feb-March.
- **Seed Rate:** 400-500 grafted/rooted plants/ha at standard spacing.
- **Spacing:** 4.5 m x 3 m or 5 m x 5 m.
- **Irrigation:** Drip irrigation, 4-8 litres/plant/day; irrigation withheld 20-25 days before bahar treatment for uniform flowering.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 625 g N, 250 g P2O5, 250 g K2O per bearing plant per year with 10-20 kg FYM, applied in split doses.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Fruit borer, thrips, fruit-sucking moth; bacterial blight (Xanthomonas), wilt, fruit rot.
- **Harvest:** Bearing starts 2-3 years after planting; fruits mature 5-7 months after flowering.
- **Expected Yield:** 12-18 tonnes/ha at full bearing.
- **Improved Varieties:** Bhagwa, Ganesh, Arakta, Mridula. Sahi dose ke liye apne KVK ya soil test se confirm karein.

**Soybean cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Kharif crop, a major oilseed of Central India (Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra).
- **Soil:** Well-drained medium black soil, pH 6.0-7.5; avoid waterlogging-prone fields.
- **Sowing Time:** Last week of June to first week of July, with monsoon onset.
- **Seed Rate:** 65-80 kg/ha of bold-seeded varieties, adjusted for germination percentage.
- **Spacing:** 45 cm x 5 cm.
- **Irrigation:** Mostly rainfed; 1-2 protective irrigations at flowering and pod filling if dry spell occurs.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 20-30:60-80:20-40 NPK kg/ha, all basal; Rhizobium japonicum and PSB seed treatment essential.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Girdle beetle, stem fly, defoliators; yellow mosaic virus, rust, Rhizoctonia root rot.
- **Harvest:** 90-110 days; harvest when 95% pods turn brown/mature colour.
- **Expected Yield:** 18-25 q/ha.
- **Improved Varieties:** JS 335, JS 95-60, NRC 37, MACS 1188, RVS 2001-4. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

**Sugarcane cultivation guide**
- **Season:** Long-duration crop (10-18 months); planted in spring, autumn or maintained as ratoon.
- **Soil:** Deep, well-drained loam to clay loam, pH 6.5-7.5, with high water and nutrient demand.
- **Sowing Time:** Spring: Feb-March; Autumn: Sept-Oct; Adsali (Maharashtra): July-Aug.
- **Seed Rate:** About 35,000-40,000 three-budded setts/ha.
- **Spacing:** Rows 90-120 cm apart; up to 150 cm for trench planting.
- **Irrigation:** 20-25 irrigations depending on season and soil; critical at germination, tillering and grand growth stage.
- **Fertilizer Schedule:** 250-300:80-100:100-120 NPK kg/ha; N in 3-4 splits, P basal, K in two splits.
- **Major Pests Diseases:** Early shoot borer, top borer, pyrilla; red rot, smut, wilt.
- **Harvest:** 10-12 months (spring), 12-18 months (adsali); harvest at peak sucrose maturity, Nov-March.
- **Expected Yield:** 700-900 q/ha (80-100 tonnes/ha).
- **Improved Varieties:** Co 0238 (CoLk 0238), Co 86032, CoS 8436, Co 0118, CoJ 64. Confirm doses with your nearest KVK or a soil test.

**Kisan Credit Card (KCC)**

The Kisan Credit Card scheme gives farmers a single, flexible short-term credit line for crop production, post-harvest expenses, farm-household consumption and maintenance of farm assets, plus a term-loan component for investments such as pump sets, land development and farm machinery. Since 2018-19 the KCC has been extended to animal husbandry, dairy and fisheries activities for working-capital needs. The card is issued as an ATM-cum-debit card (RuPee KCC card) with a validity of five years and an annual step-up in the credit limit.

**Benefit:** Crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh at an effective interest rate of 4% per annum for prompt repayers: the base rate of 7% is reduced by a 1.5% interest subvention to banks and a further 3% Prompt Repayment Incentive to the farmer. From 2025-26 the collateral-free limit was raised to Rs 2 lakh per borrower, and the modified interest subvention limit for KCC crop loans was enhanced to Rs 5 lakh. Animal husbandry and fisheries KCC holders get the same concessional treatment within a sub-limit (commonly Rs 2 lakh).

**Eligibility:** All farmers - individual or joint cultivators who are owner-cultivators, oral lessees, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, and members of Joint Liability Groups or Self Help Groups. Also available to dairy, poultry, goatery, piggery, inland fishery and marine fishery operators. Applicants must have a bank account and valid identity, address and land/activity documents.

**Apply:** Apply at any commercial bank, regional rural bank, small finance bank, or cooperative bank branch, or online through the bank's website or the Jan Samarth portal https://www.jansamarth.in. A simplified one-page KCC form is available on the PM-KISAN portal, and banks are required to dispose of complete applications within 14 days. Documents: filled application, Aadhaar/PAN, passport photograph, land ownership or tenancy proof, and a no-dues certificate from other banks.

**National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM)**

NBHM was launched in 2020 under the Atmanirbhar Bharat package to promote scientific beekeeping as a means of increasing crop productivity through pollination and of raising farm incomes through honey and other hive products. It has three mini-missions covering promotion and production, post-harvest management and processing including honey testing labs, and research and technology generation. The mission promotes the 'Sweet Revolution' and honey traceability through the Madhukranti portal.

**Benefit:** Assistance for bee colonies, bee boxes/hives, honey extractors, food-grade containers and other beekeeping equipment (commonly 75-90% assistance for beekeepers/FPOs/SHGs depending on category and component); support for setting up Integrated Beekeeping Development Centres, honey testing laboratories, custom hiring centres for beekeeping equipment, cold chains and processing units; and training and capacity building of beekeepers.

**Eligibility:** Individual beekeepers, farmers, entrepreneurs, Self Help Groups, Farmer Producer Organisations, cooperatives, NGOs, state agencies, agricultural universities and research institutions engaged in or intending to take up beekeeping.

**Apply:** Register on the Madhukranti portal at https://www.nbb.gov.in / https://madhukranti.in and submit the project proposal to the National Bee Board through the State Bee Board, state horticulture/agriculture department or an implementing agency. Proposals are appraised by the Executive Committee of the National Bee Board and assistance is released to the beneficiary/implementing agency.

**Corn : Northern Leaf Blight**

Northern corn leaf blight (NCLB) is caused by the fungus Setosphaeria turcica. Symptoms usually appear first on the lower leaves. Leaf lesions are long (1 to 6 inches) and elliptical, gray-green at first but then turn pale gray or tan. Under moist conditions, dark gray spores are produced, usually on the lower leaf surface, which give lesions a "dirty" gray appearance. Entire leaves on severely blighted plants can die, so individual lesions are not visible. Lesions may occur on the outer husk of ears, but the kernels are not infected. On hybrids that contain an Ht gene for resistance to the fungus, lesions are smaller, chlorotic, and may develop into linear streaks. These lesions rarely produce spores.

**Prevention and treatment:** Fungicide applications reduced Northern Corn Leaf Blight damage and protected yield. Fungicide value was higher in reducing yield in susceptible corn hybrids. Fungicide were most effective if they were applied at disease onset. Disease onset varied in growth stages, and so the best stage to apply fungicides.

**Grape : Black Rot**

Grape black rot is a fungal disease caused by an ascomycetous fungus, Guignardia bidwellii, that attacks grape vines during hot and humid weather. “Grape black rot originated in eastern North America, but now occurs in portions of Europe, South America, and Asia. It can cause complete crop loss in warm, humid climates, but is virtually unknown in regions with arid summers.” The name comes from the black fringe that borders growing brown patches on the leaves. The disease also attacks other parts of the plant, “all green parts of the vine: the shoots, leaf and fruit stems, tendrils, and fruit. The most damaging effect is to the fruit”

**Prevention and treatment:** Mancozeb is available as BONIDE MANCOZEB FLOWABLE fungicide. It contains 37% Mancozeb and should be very effective for controlling black rot. Nova (myclobutanil) is available in IMMUNOX FUNGICIDE. It is 1.55 % myclobutanil and should be effective for controlling black rot.

**Strawberry : Leaf Scorch**

Leaf scorch symptoms are very similar to the early stages of common (Mycosphaerella) leaf spot, with irregular dark purple spots being scattered over the upper leaf surface. As the spots enlarge, they begin to look like drops of tar, and are actually the accumulations of black fruiting bodies (acervuli) of the fungus. The centers of the spots remain purple (in Mycosphaerella leaf spot they are white) and there is no well-defined lesion border. In heavy infections, these regions coalesce and the tissue between the lesions often takes on a purplish to bright red color that is dependent on cultivar, temperature, or other factors. The leaves eventually turn brown, dry up, and curl at the margins giving the leaf a scorched appearance. Examination of the acervuli and conidial morphology can help to distinguish between leaf spot and leaf scorch at this advanced stage of disease. On the upper leaf surfaces of leaf scorch lesions, the acervuli are dark with glistening spore masses and dark apothecia. Petiole lesions are elongate, sunken, with a purplish to brown color and can kill the leaf by girdling the petiole. Runners, fruit stalks, fruit and caps can also become infected. Plants may become weakened and the number and vigor of crowns reduced. Infection predisposes the plants to winter and drought stress. In severe infestations, flowers and fruit may die.

**Prevention and treatment:** While leaf scorch on strawberry plants can be frustrating, there are some strategies which home gardeners may employ to help prevent its spread in the garden. The primary means of strawberry leaf scorch control should always be prevention. Since this fungal pathogen overwinters on the fallen leaves of infected plants, proper garden sanitation is key. This includes the removal of infected garden debris from the strawberry patch, as well as the frequent establishment of new strawberry transplants. The creation of new plantings and strawberry patches is key to maintaining a consistent strawberry harvest, as older plants are more likely to show signs of severe infection.

**Tomato : Bacterial Spot**

Bacterial spot of tomato is a potentially devastating disease that, in severe cases, can lead to unmarketable fruit and even plant death.  Bacterial spot can occur wherever tomatoes are grown, but is found most frequently in warm, wet climates, as well as in greenhouses.  The disease is often an issue in Wisconsin.Bacterial spot can affect all above ground parts of a tomato plant, including the leaves, stems, and fruit.  Bacterial spot appears on leaves as small (less than ? inch), sometimes water-soaked (i.e., wet-looking) circular areas.  Spots may initially be yellow-green, but darken to brownish-red as they age.  When the disease is severe, extensive leaf yellowing and leaf loss can also occur.  On green fruit, spots are typically small, raised and blister-like, and may have a yellowish halo.  As fruit mature, the spots enlarge (reaching a maximum size of ¼ inch) and turn brown, scabby and rough.  Mature spots may be raised, or sunken with raised edges.

**Prevention and treatment:** Plant pathogen-free seed or transplants to prevent the introduction of bacterial spot pathogens on contaminated seed or seedlings.  If a clean seed source is not available or you suspect that your seed is contaminated, soak seeds in water at 122°F for 25 min. to kill the pathogens.  To keep leaves dry and to prevent the spread of the pathogens, avoid overhead watering (e.g., with a wand or sprinkler) of established plants and instead use a drip-tape or soaker-hose.  Also to prevent spread, DO NOT handle plants when they are wet (e.g., from dew) and routinely sterilize tools with either 10% bleach solution or (better) 70% alcohol (e.g., rubbing alcohol).  Where bacterial spot has been a recurring problem, consider using preventative applications of copper-based products registered for use on tomato, especially during warm, wet periods.  Keep in mind however, that if used excessively or for prolonged periods, copper may no longer control the disease. The disease spreads quickly in fields and can result in total crop failure if untreated.

Clean up all debris and fallen fruit from the garden area. This is particularly essential in warmer areas where extended freezing is unlikely and the late blight tomato disease may overwinter in the fallen fruit. Currently, there are no strains of tomato available that are resistant to late tomato blight, so plants should be inspected at least twice a week. Since late blight symptoms are more likely to occur during wet conditions, more care should be taken during those times. Repeated applications are necessary throughout the growing season as the disease can strike at any time. For organic gardeners, there are some fixed copper products approved for use; otherwise, all infected plants must be immediately removed and destroyed.", "image_url": "https://www.canr.msu.edu/contentAsset/image/e97d1ef0-5b55-49b0-ab4e-c57dcbeca65e/fileAsset/filter/Resize,Jpeg/resize_w/750/jpeg_q/80", "supplement": {"name": "ACROBAT FUNGICIDE", "image": "https://encrypted-tbn3.gstatic.com/shopping?q=tbn:ANd9GcRpQmIM9QZkFI43PPlHVFaSlGdrdMP8LFHXAo9b_OGOQCi3R6G-SsqnCXFR4CU9bVAcyuBGTrQRAkRrU9fm-1TGeXg9PrsB&usqp=CAE", "buy_link": "https://www.bighaat.com/products/acrobat-fungicide?variant=31177935519767&currency=INR&utm_medium=product_sync&utm_source=google&utm_content=sag_organic&utm_campaign=sag_organic"}}

**Tomato : Late Blight**

Late blight is caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans. Oomycetes are fungus-like organisms also called water molds, but they are not true fungi.
There are many different strains of P. infestans. These are called clonal lineages and designated by a number code (i.e. US-23). Many clonal lineages affect both tomato and potato, but some lineages are specific to one host or the other.Late blight is a potentially devastating disease of tomato and potato, infecting leaves, stems and fruits of tomato plants.
The disease spreads quickly in fields and can result in total crop failure if untreated.
Late blight of potato was responsible for the Irish potato famine of the late 1840s.

**Prevention and treatment:** Sanitation is the first step in controlling tomato late blight. Clean up all debris and fallen fruit from the garden area. This is particularly essential in warmer areas where extended freezing is unlikely and the late blight tomato disease may overwinter in the fallen fruit. Currently, there are no strains of tomato available that are resistant to late tomato blight, so plants should be inspected at least twice a week. Since late blight symptoms are more likely to occur during wet conditions, more care should be taken during those times. For the home gardener, fungicides that contain maneb, mancozeb, chlorothanolil or fixed copper can help protect plants from late tomato blight. Repeated applications are necessary throughout the growing season as the disease can strike at any time. For organic gardeners, there are some fixed copper products approved for use; otherwise, all infected plants must be immediately removed and destroyed.

**Tomato : Spider Mites | Two-Spotted Spider Mite**

The two-spotted spider mite is the most common mite species that attacks vegetable and fruit crops in New England. Spider mites can occur in tomato, eggplant, potato, vine crops such as melons, cucumbers, and other crops. Two-spotted spider mites are one of the most important pests of eggplant. They have up to 20 generations per year and are favored by excess nitrogen and dry and dusty conditions. Outbreaks are often caused by the use of broad-spectrum insecticides which interfere with the numerous natural enemies that help to manage mite populations. As with most pests, catching the problem early will mean easier control.

**Prevention and treatment:** Avoid weedy fields and do not plant eggplant adjacent to legume forage crops.
Avoid early season, broad-spectrum insecticide applications for other pests.
Do not over-fertilize.
Overhead irrigation or prolonged periods of rain can help reduce populations.

Spread to all leaflets and to other leaves is rapid , causing the leaves to turn yellow, collapse and die . Spots also occur on the stems. They are long and thin. Small light brown spots with dark margins may also occur on the fruit.
The spores are spread by wind-blown rain, and if windy wet weather continues for a few days, spread is fast and plants lose their leaves quickly.", "prevention": "Cultural control is important. The following should be done:
Do not plant new crops next to older ones that have the disease.

**Tomato : Target Spot**

The disease starts on the older leaves and spreads upwards. The first signs are irregular-shaped spots (less than 1 mm) with a yellow margin . Some of the spots enlarge up to 10 mm and show characteristics rings, hence the name of "target spot" . Spread to all leaflets and to other leaves is rapid , causing the leaves to turn yellow, collapse and die . Spots also occur on the stems. They are long and thin. Small light brown spots with dark margins may also occur on the fruit.
The spores are spread by wind-blown rain, and if windy wet weather continues for a few days, spread is fast and plants lose their leaves quickly.

**Prevention and treatment:** Cultural control is important. The following should be done:
Do not plant new crops next to older ones that have the disease.
Plant as far as possible from papaya, especially if leaves have small angular spots (Photo 5).
Check all seedlings in the nursery, and throw away any with leaf spots.
Remove a few branches from the lower part of the plants to allow better airflow at the base
Remove and burn the lower leaves as soon as the disease is seen, especially after the lower fruit trusses have been picked.
Keep plots free from weeds, as some may be hosts of the fungus.
Do not use overhead irrigation; otherwise, it will create conditions for spore production and infection.
Collect and burn as much of the crop as possible when the harvest is complete.
Practise crop rotation, leaving 3 years before replanting tomato on the same land.

Hybrid seeds: Hybrid seeds are produced by cross-breeding two or more distinct plant varieties to create a new variety with desirable traits, such as disease and pest resistance. Genetically modified (GM) seeds: GM seeds have been genetically altered to express certain traits, such as resistance to specific pests or diseases. For example, Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) maize has been genetically modified to produce a protein toxic to certain insect pests. Heirloom or heritage seeds: Heirloom or heritage seeds are non-hybrid seeds that have been passed down from generation to generation, often for centuries. These seeds have developed natural resistance to local pests and diseases over time. Open-pollinated seeds: Open-pollinated seeds are non-hybrid seeds that have been pollinated by natural means, such as wind or insects. These seeds can be genetically diverse and may exhibit natural resistance to pests and diseases.

function.name: recommend_crop
function.description: Recommend the best crop to grow from soil test values and climate. Use when the farmer gives N, P, K, temperature, humidity, pH and rainfall numbers (ask for any that are missing).

function.name: recommend_fertilizer
function.description: Recommend a commercial fertilizer (Urea, DAP, 10-26-26, 14-35-14, 17-17-17, 20-20, 28-28) by working out the crop's nutrient requirement, subtracting what the soil test already supplies, and matching the remaining N-P2O5-K2O ratio against each product. Returns the pick, a one-line reason, the ranked top 3 and the kg/ha deficit; pass area to also get the dose in kg and 50-kg bags. soil_type must be one of ['Black', 'Clayey', 'Loamy', 'Red', 'Sandy']; crop_type one of ['Barley', 'Cotton', 'Ground Nuts', 'Maize', 'Millets', 'Oil seeds', 'Paddy', 'Pulses', 'Sugarcane', 'Tobacco', 'Wheat']. N, K and P are available soil nutrients in kg/ha (Soil Health Card values).

area.description: Field area (optional) - adds a dose calculation

function.name: predict_yield
function.description: Estimate crop yield (tonnes/hectare) for an Indian state and season from a model trained on 1997-2020 state-level records. Returns the point estimate, a 10-90% expected_range and baseline_yield (the 5-year median for that crop and state) so the farmer can see whether the model is saying anything new. Never invent fertilizer or pesticide figures: leave them out and regional medians are used, and the result reports which values it fell back on. Do NOT pass production - yield is derived from production in the source data, so supplying it would just echo the answer back. Call get_reference_lists first if unsure about valid crop/state/season names.

season.description: Kharif, Rabi, Whole Year, Summer, Autumn or Winter

fertilizer.description: Total fertilizer used in kg (optional; omit if unknown)

pesticide.description: Total pesticide used in kg (optional; omit if unknown)

function.name: get_reference_lists
function.description: Return valid crop, state and season names accepted by predict_yield, plus supported crops for the fertilizer calculator.

function.name: fertilizer_calculator
function.description: Compute how many kg / 50-kg bags of Urea, DAP and MOP a farmer needs for a crop and field area, with a split-application schedule. Optionally adjust for soil-test values.

soil_n.description: Available soil N kg/ha from soil health card (optional)

Returns the point estimate, a 10-90% expected_range and baseline_yield (the 5-year median for that crop and state) so the farmer can see whether the model is saying anything new. Never invent fertilizer or pesticide figures: leave them out and regional medians are used, and the result reports which values it fell back on. Do NOT pass production - yield is derived from production in the source data, so supplying it would just echo the answer back. Call get_reference_lists first if unsure about valid crop/state/season names.

N, K and P are available soil nutrients in kg/ha (Soil Health Card values).

area.description: Field area (optional) - adds a dose calculation

function.name: predict_yield
function.description: Estimate crop yield (tonnes/hectare) for an Indian state and season from a model trained on 1997-2020 state-level records. Returns the point estimate, a 10-90% expected_range and baseline_yield (the 5-year median for that crop and state) so the farmer can see whether the model is saying anything new. Never invent fertilizer or pesticide figures: leave them out and regional medians are used, and the result reports which values it fell back on. Do NOT pass production - yield is derived from production in the source data, so supplying it would just echo the answer back. Call get_reference_lists first if unsure about valid crop/state/season names.

Returns the point estimate, a 10-90% expected_range and baseline_yield (the 5-year median for that crop and state) so the farmer can see whether the model is saying anything new. Never invent fertilizer or pesticide figures: leave them out and regional medians are used, and the result reports which values it fell back on. Do NOT pass production - yield is derived from production in the source data, so supplying it would just echo the answer back. Bhaiya ji, is it profitable to grow leafy veg like coriander between muskmelon beds? How much seed is needed?

Yes, growing coriander (dhaniya) as an intercrop between muskmelon (kharbuja) beds is **quite profitable and a smart agronomic practice**. 

### Why It Works Well:
1. **Quick Returns:** Coriander takes only 35–45 days to harvest, giving you an early cash flow before the muskmelon (approx. 90-day duration) spreads completely over the beds.
2. **Pest Control Benefit:** Coriander flowers and foliage attract beneficial predatory insects (like hoverflies and coccinellid beetles) that help manage aphids and other pests naturally in your field.
3. **Efficient Land Use:** Muskmelon is typically planted in raised beds or furrows, leaving the channels or inter-row spaces empty initially. Coriander fits nicely into this gap without competing heavily for nutrients if fertilized properly.

### Seed Rate:
* **For intercropping** (sowing only in the spaces/strips between muskmelon beds), you will need about **8 to 10 kg of coriander seeds per acre**. 
* Make sure to split the seeds gently (crush them lightly into two halves) before sowing for faster and uniform germination.

### Quick Tips for Success:
* **Sowing Time:** Best sown during the Zaid season (January to March) along with your muskmelon.
* **Fertilizer Note:** Muskmelon requires a balanced dose (around 100 kg N, 50 kg P₂O₅, and 50 kg K₂O per hectare). Ensure you apply adequate base fertilizers so neither crop faces nutrient deficiency.
* **Harvesting:** Harvest the coriander as leafy greens before the muskmelon vines start trailing heavily across the beds.

अहो साहेब, लातूरहून बोलतो. सफरचंदाच्या झाडाला डीएपी आणि युरियाचा डोस द्यायची अचूक पद्धत कोणती आहे?

राम राम साहेब, लातूरहून बोलत आहात. 

सर्वात महत्त्वाची गोष्ट म्हणजे **लातूरच्या उष्ण आणि कोरड्या हवामानात सफरचंदाची (Apple) शेती व्यावसायिक दृष्टिकोनातून यशस्वी होत नाही**, कारण सफरचंदाच्या झाडांना फळ धरण्यासाठी आणि चांगल्या वाढीसाठी 'चिलिंग आवर्स'ची (थंड हवेची) गरज असते, जे लातूरमध्ये उपलब्ध नसतात. कदाचित आपल्या भागात **बटाटा (Potato)** किंवा इतर फळझाडे (उदा. सीताफळ, डाळिंब) लावली असतील. बटाट्यासाठी डीएपी आणि युरियाचा डोस कसा द्यावा, याची माहिती खालीलप्रमाणे आहे:

### बटाटा पिकासाठी डीएपी आणि युरिया देण्याची अचूक पद्धत:

* **वेळ:** खतांचा अर्धा डोस आणि पूर्ण डीएपी **लागवडीच्या वेळी (बेसल डोस)** जमिनीत द्यावा आणि उरलेला युरियाचा डोस **पहिल्या माती भरणीच्या वेळी (लागवडीनंतर सुमारे ३०-३५ दिवसांनी)** द्यावा.
* **मात्रा (प्रति एकर):** 
  * डीएपी: साधारण ५० ते ६० किलो (एकरी)
  * युरिया: साधारण ४० ते ५० किलो (एकरी)
* **पद्धत:**
  1. **लागवडीच्या वेळी:** सरीमध्ये किंवा वाफ्यात बियाणे ठेवण्यापूर्वी डीएपी मातीत चांगले मिसळून घ्यावे, जेणेकरून खत थेट बटाट्याच्या कंदाला चिकटणार नाही (रासायनिक बाधेपासून रक्षण होते).
  2. **दुसरा डोस (युरिया):** झाडांची वाढ होत असताना (३०-३५ दिवसांनी) रोपांच्या बाजूने मातीत युरिया पेरून हलकी माती भरून द्यावी आणि लगेच पाणी द्यावे.

जर आपण **सफरचंद** ऐवजी दुसऱ्या कोणत्या फळझाडाबद्दल विचारत असाल, तर कृपया त्या झाडाचे नाव सांगा, जेणेकरून योग्य डोस सांगता येईल. तसेच खते खरेदी करण्यासाठी आपण [KrishiDisha मार्केटप्लेस](/marketplace/product/) ला भेट देऊ शकता.

Symptoms: Water-soaked lesions form on leaf margins turning brown-black with white fungal growth on the undersurface in humid weather; tubers show reddish-brown dry rot.. Management: Use disease-free seed tubers, earth up properly and avoid overhead irrigation in cloudy weather; spray mancozeb 75 WP @ 2.5 g/litre prophylactically and cymoxanil + mancozeb @ 3 g/litre on disease appearance.", "source": "Integrated pest management guide", "score": 0.373, "kind": "pest"}, {"id": "disease:22", "title": "Potato : Late Blight", "text": "Potato : Late Blight. These lesions usually appear first on the lower leaves. Lesions often begin to develop near the leaf tips or edges, where dew is retained the longest.During cool, moist weather, these lesions expand rapidly into large, dark brown or black lesions, often appearing greasy. Leaf lesions also frequently are surrounded by a yellow chlorotic halo Prevention and treatment: The severe late blight can be effectively managed with prophylactic spray of mancozeb at 0.25% followed by cymoxanil+mancozeb or dimethomorph+mancozeb at 0.3% at the onset of disease and one more spray of mancozeb at 0.25% seven days after application of systemic fungicides in West Bengal ", "source": "PlantVillage disease guide", "score": 0.225, "kind": "disease", "index": 22}, {"id": "disease:31", "title": "Tomato : Late Blight", "text": "Tomato : Late Blight. Late blight is caused by the oomycete Phytophthora infestans. Oomycetes are fungus-like organisms also called water molds, but they are not true fungi.
There are many different strains of P. infestans. These are called clonal lineages and designated by a number code (i.e. US-23). Many clonal lineages affect both tomato and potato, but some lineages are specific to one host or the other.Late blight is a potentially devastating disease of tomato and potato, infecting leaves, stems and fruits of tomato plants.
The disease spreads quickly in fields and can result in total crop failure if untreated.
Late blight of potato was responsible for the Irish potato famine of the late 1840s. Prevention and treatment: Sanitation is the first step in controlling tomato late blight. Clean up all debris and fallen fruit from the garden area. This is particularly essential in warmer areas where extended freezing is unlikely and the late blight tomato disease may overwinter in the fallen fruit. Currently, there are no strains of tomato available that are resistant to late tomato blight, so plants should be inspected at least twice a week. Since late blight symptoms are more likely to occur during wet conditions, more care should be taken during those times. For the home gardener, fungicides that contain maneb, mancozeb, chlorothanolil or fixed copper can help protect plants from late tomato blight. వాతావరణం మేఘావృతంగా, తేలికగా ఉంటే **ఆలుగడ్డకు తెగులు (లేట్ బ్లైట్) రాకపోవడానికి మందు కొట్టడం చాలా అవసరం**.

**ప్రోఫిలాక్టిక్ స్ప్రే (అనుమానంగా ముందుగానే):**
- **మాన్కోజೆబ్ 75 WP** – 2.5 గ్రాము / లిటర్ నీళ్లు  
  (ఏకరుకు 200 లిటర్ స్ప్రే ద్రవ్యం → 500 గ్రాము మాన్కోజెబ్)

**వ్యాధి కనిపిస్తే (వైపు చెట్టుల పై మిగిలిన తెగులలో വെళ్లగా స్ఫటికాలు చూపిస్తే):**
- **సిమాక్సానిల్ + మాన్కోజెబ్** – 3 గ్రాము / లిటర్  
  (ఏకరుకు 200 లిటర్ → 600 గ్రాము)

**సావధానులు:**
- స్ప్రే సున్నీగా లేదా సాయంత్రం చేయండి (మధ్యాహ్న வெడి నివారించుకోండి).
- ముక్కు, కన్ను, కైలు కవర్ చేయి (మాస్క్, గ్లవ్స్, గాజుల్స్) ఉపయోగించండి.
- ఫసల్ కోసుకునే 7 రోజుల ముందు చివరి స్ప్రే ముగించాలి (PHI).
- సస్యాల మధ్య వాతావరణ ఉచితంగా వహించుకోవల్సిన ఎత్తు (60×20 సెం.మీ) ఉంచుకోండి.
- మൂടి నీళ్ళు నిలవడాన్ని నివారించుకోండి.

**ఆర్గానిక్ ఎంపిక:** కాపర్ ఆక్సీక్లోరైడ్ 50 WP – 3 గ్రాము / లిటర్ (సప్తాహానికి ఒకసారి).

For kidney beans (rajma) in high-alkaline soil, apply **neem cake 15–20 days before sowing**.

**Why this timing**
- Neem cake needs 2–3 weeks to decompose and release organic acids that start buffering the high pH.
- It also acts as a bio-fumigant against soil-borne fungi (anthracnose, root rots) common in rajma.
- Applying at basal fertiliser time (full NPK dose is basal for rajma) lets you incorporate both together.

**Dose & method**
- **Rate:** 250–500 kg/acre (1–2 quintal/acre)
- **Incorporation:** Broadcast evenly, mix into top 15–20 cm soil with a cultivator/rotavator.
- **Irrigation:** Give one light irrigation after mixing to kick-start microbial activity.

**Extra tips for alkaline soil**
- Add **gypsum @ 250–500 kg/acre** along with neem cake if soil test shows high ESP (exchangeable sodium %).
- Use **acid-forming fertilisers** (DAP, ammonium sulphate) for the basal P & N dose.
- Choose a variety tolerant to alkalinity (e.g., **PDR 14, VL Rajma 63**).
- Target soil pH 6.0–7.5; re-check after 1 season.

**Sowing window reminder** (from the calendar)
- **Rabi (plains):** Oct–Nov  
- **Kharif (hills):** Apr–May

Apply neem cake accordingly so it’s fully decomposed by your chosen sowing date.

साब, 2 एकड़ में बाजरा बोया है, पानी कब-कब देना चाहिए ताकि फसल सूखे ना?

राम-राम साब! बाजरा (Pearl millet) सूखा सहन करने वाली फसल है, लेकिन अधिक पैदावार के लिए इसकी संवेदनशील अवस्थाओं (Critical stages) पर सिंचाई करना बहुत जरूरी है ताकि फसल सूखे से बचे। 

आपके 2 एकड़ बाजरा के खेत के लिए सिंचाई का सही शेड्यूल नीचे दिया गया है:

### बाजरा में सिंचाई की मुख्य अवस्थाएं:

1. **पहली सिंचाई (कल्ले फूटने की अवस्था - Tillering):** बुवाई के **20 से 25 दिन बाद** पहली हल्की सिंचाई करें। इस समय पौधे जड़ें फैलाते हैं और कल्ले निकलते हैं।
2. **दूसरी और सबसे महत्वपूर्ण सिंचाई (बालियां निकलते समय - Booting / Flowering):** बुवाई के **40 से 45 दिन बाद** जब बालियां निकल रही हों या फूल आ रहे हों, तब नमी होना सबसे जरूरी है। इस अवस्था में पानी की कमी होने पर दाने नहीं बनते और पैदावार घट जाती है।
3. **तीसरी सिंचाई (दाना भरने की अवस्था - Grain filling):** बुवाई के **60 से 65 दिन बाद** जब दाने सख्त हो रहे हों, तब एक हल्की सिंचाई और दें ताकि दाने मोटे और पुष्ट बनें।

### जरूरी बातें:
- **जल निकास:** बाजरा जलभराव (Waterlogging) बिल्कुल सहन नहीं कर सकता, इसलिए खेत में पानी रुकने न दें। अच्छी जल निकासी का प्रबंध रखें।
- यदि वर्षा समय पर हो रही हो तो सिंचाई की आवश्यकता कम होगी, लेकिन सूखे (Dry spell) की स्थिति में उपर्युक्त अवस्थाओं पर पानी अवश्य लगाएं। 

फसल से जुड़ी किसी अन्य जानकारी (जैसे खाद प्रबंधन या कीट नियंत्रण) के लिए बेझिझक पूछें!

heavy dew fall is happening in the morning this week, will it cause yellow rust in my pulses?

Heavy morning dew creates high relative humidity and leaf wetness, which **favour fungal diseases**, but **yellow rust does not affect pulses**. 

### Will yellow rust affect your pulses?
No. Yellow (stripe) rust is a specific disease that affects **wheat**, not pulse crops like gram (chana), moong, or urad. 

### What to watch out for in pulses during heavy dew:
While your pulses are safe from yellow rust, high morning moisture and fog can trigger other fungal and pest problems in pulses, such as:
1. **Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera):** Thrives in humid, cloudy weather. Monitor flowers and young pods.
2. **Powdery Mildew or Collar Rot:** Can develop if fields remain waterlogged or lack proper air circulation.

### Recommended Precautions:
* **Monitor fields regularly:** Check the lower leaves and canopy edges early in the morning for any white/grey fungal patches or pest larvae.
* **Avoid excess irrigation:** With heavy dew providing moisture, hold off on watering unless the soil is dry.
* **Fungicide/Pest management:** If you notice early signs of fungal infection or pod borers, use recommended protective sprays. You can check suitable products on the [KrishiDisha Marketplace](/marketplace/product/). 

*Safety tip: Always wear protective gear (gloves, mask) when applying sprays, and check the pre-harvest interval before application.*

நம்ம நிலத்தோட மண்ணு தரத்த வச்சு, இந்த தடவை நெல் ஈல்டு எவ்வளவுக்கு போகும்னு ஒரு அંદાது சொல்ல முடியுமா சார்?

வணக்கம்! நிச்சயமாக உங்கள் நிலத்தில் நெல் (Paddy) சாகுபடி செய்தால் எவ்வளவு மகசூல் (Yield) கிடைக்கும் என்பதை நாம் மதிப்பிடலாம். 

இதற்கு எனக்கு சில விவரங்கள் தேவைப்படுகின்றன:

1. **மாநிலம் மற்றும் மாவட்டம்** (எ.கா: தமிழ்நாடு, தஞ்சாவூர்)
2. **பயிரிடும் பரப்பளவு** (எத்தனை ஏக்கர் அல்லது ஹெக்டேர்?)
3. **பருவம் மற்றும் ஆண்டு** (எ.கா: குறுவை, சம்பா / 2024 அல்லது 2025)
4. **ஆண்டு மழை அளவு** (தோராயமாக மிமீ-ல்)
5. உங்களது **மண் பரிசோதனை முடிவு** (Soil Health Card) இருந்தால், அதில் உள்ள தழைச்சத்து (N), மணிச்சத்து (P), சாம்பல் சத்து (K) மற்றும் pH மதிண்களைச் சொல்லுங்கள்.

இந்த விவரங்களைக் கொடுத்தால், நமது மகசூல் கணிப்பு (Yield Prediction) கருவி மூலம் மிகத் துல்லியமான அத்து அண்மதிப்பை (Estimate) உங்களுக்குக் கணக்கிட்டுச் சொல்ல முடியும்!

Ji, maine suna hai ki amrapali mango ki variety chhote jagah me acchi hoti hai, kya mai apne 2 acre me ise laga sakta hu?

Haan bilkul! Aap apne **2 acre** mein **Amrapali mango** ki variety bahut aasani se laga sakte hain. 

Amrapali ek dwarf (chhoti) variety hai, isliye ise high-density planting mein lagaya jata hai. Aaiye iski puri jaankari dekhte hain:

### 1. Planting & Spacing (Duri aur Paudhe)
* **Spacing:** Amrapali ke liye **2.5 m × 2.5 m** ya **3 m × 3 m** ki duri sabse acchi hoti hai.
* **Paudhe per acre:** 2.5 × 2.5 metre ki duri par lagane se ek acre mein lagbhag **640 paudhe** aate hain, yaani 2 acre mein **1280 paudhe** lagenge. (Purani lambi varieties ke mukable yahan aap bahut zyada paudhe laga sakte hain).

### 2. Fertilizer Schedule (Khaad Schedule - per hectare ke aadhar par)
* Mango ke liye recommended dose **100 kg N, 50 kg P₂O₅, aur 100 kg K₂O per hectare** hoti hai. Isko aap apne 2 acre ke khet ke hisaab se divide kar sakte hain.
* Har saal June-July (baarish ke shuruat mein) organic khaad (FYM) aur basic fertilizers dena zaroori hai.

### 3. Disease Management (Rog Niyantran)
* **Powdery Mildew (Safed Fafund):** Isse phool aur chhote phal jhadne lagte hain. 
* **R रोकथाम (Cure):** Panicle (manjar) nikalne ke samay **wettable sulphur 80 WP @ 2 gram per litre** ya **hexaconazole 5 EC @ 2 ml per litre** ka spray karein. Zaroorat padne par 15 din baad dobara spray karein. Hawa aane ke liye ped ki halki pruning bhi zaroori hai.

Agar aapko Amrapali ke paudhe, wettable sulphur, ya hexaconazole kharidne hain, toh aap hamare [KrishiDisha Marketplace](/marketplace/product/) par check kar sakte hain. 

Kya aapko iske gaddhe khodne ke tareeqe ya sinchai (irrigation) ke baare mein kuch aur jaan na hai?

Bhaiya, neem oil kitna ml per pump dalna chahiye chana me pod borer ke liye? And organic me koi aur acha dawa hai kya?

### Pod Borer Management in Chickpea (Chana)

For controlling **pod borer (*Helicoverpa armigera*)** in chickpea, here are the recommended organic options and doses:

#### 1. Neem Oil (Organic)
* **Dose:** **30 to 50 ml per 15-litre knapsack pump** (or 5 ml per litre of water). 
* **Tips:** Use a good quality 10,000 ppm neem oil and add a few drops of liquid soap as a sticker so it spreads well on the leaves and pods. Spray in the early morning or late evening.

#### 2. Other Organic / Biological Options
* **NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus):** Apply **HaNPV @ 250 LE per hectare** (approx. 100 LE per acre) during evening hours. It specifically targets pod borer larvae.
* **Pheromone Traps:** Install **5 traps per hectare** to monitor and trap adult moths early.
* **Bird Perches:** Set up 20-25 bird perches per hectare to invite insectivorous birds that feed on the larvae.
* **Bt (*Bacillus thuringiensis*):** You can also spray commercial formulations of *Bt* as per product instructions when larvae are small.

#### Marketplace Products
You can check organic neem oil and pest control inputs on our [KrishiDisha Marketplace](/marketplace/product/neem-oil-1l).

அய்யா, உருளைக்கிழங்கு விலை ஏறும் போது விநியோகம் பண்ண இந்த FPO மூலமா குளிர்படன் வசதி கிடைக்குமா?

**உருளைக்கிழங்கு விலை உயர்ந்தால் FPO‑வின் மூலம் குளிர்பதன வசதி பெறும் வழிகள்**  

1. **FPO‑யில் சேர்ந்து கூட்டாக செயல்படுங்கள்**  
   - 2020‑ல் தொடங்கப்பட்ட **“10,000 FPO Formation & Promotion”** (Rs 6,865 crore) திட்டம், சிறிய வேளாண் உற்பத்தியாளர்களை ஒன்றிணைத்து உள்ளீடு, சந்தை, சேமிப்பு (cold‑chain) போன்ற வசதிகளை எளிதில் பெற உதவுகிறது【Government scheme directory】.  

2. **குளிர்பதன வசதி (Cold‑Chain) திட்டங்கள்**  
   - **NABARD Cold‑Storage Scheme** – FPO‑கள், கூட்டுத்தொகை (joint‑venture) அல்லது ஒப்பந்த (PPP) முறையில் 10 %‑30 % நிதி உதவி பெறலாம்.  
   - **மாநில‑மட்டம் குளிர்பதன மையங்கள்** – உங்கள் மாவட்டம்/மாநிலம் வழங்கும் “குளிர்பதன மையம்” (Cold Storage) திட்டங்களை (அதிகம் AGRI‑INFRA, MSME) பார்க்கவும்.  

3. **விநியோகத்திற்காக Kisan Rail / Krishi UDAN**  
   - **Kisan Rail** மற்றும் **Krishi UDAN** திட்டங்கள், குளிர்பதனக் கோச்சுகள் (refrigerated coaches) உடன் பழம்‑காய்கறி, உருளைக்கிழங்கு போன்ற பச்சை பொருட்களை விரைவாக நகர்த்த உதவுகின்றன【Government scheme directory】.  

4. **e‑NAM மூலம் நேரடி விற்பனை**  
   - **e‑NAM** (National Agriculture Market)‑ல் உங்கள் FPO‑யை பதிவு செய்து, ஆன்லைன் bidding, assaying‑based price discovery, நேரடி வங்கி பணம் பெறுதல் ஆகியவற்றை பயன்படுத்தலாம்【Government scheme directory】.  

5. **நடவடிக்கை படி**  
   - **①** அருகிலுள்ள FPO‑யில் (அல்லது உங்கள் சொந்த FPO‑யை தொடங்க) உறுப்பினர் ஆகுங்கள்.  
   - **②** NABARD‑இன் Cold‑Storage Scheme‑க்கு விண்ணப்பம் (project proposal, land document, financial capacity) சமர்ப்பிக்கவும்.  
   - **③** மாநிலம்/மாநில விவசாயத் துறையின் “Cold‑Storage Subsidy” அறிவிப்புகளை (விண்ணப்ப காலம், ஆவணங்கள்) கண்காணித்து, தேவையான ஆதரவைப் பெறுங்கள்.  
   - **④** Kisan Rail / Krishi UDAN‑இல் பதிவு செய்து, குளிர்பதனக் கோச்சில் உருளைக்கிழங்கை இலக்கு சந்தைக்கு (மண்டி/e‑NAM) கொண்டு செல்லுங்கள்.  
   - **⑤** e‑NAM‑ல் உங்கள் FPO‑யை பதிவு செய்து, ஆன்லைன் bidding‑ல் பங்கேற்று, உயர்ந்த விலையுடன் விற்பனை செய்யுங்கள்.  

**கவனிக்க வேண்டியவை**  
- குளிர்பதன மையம் கட்டும் போது, மின்சாரம் (solar backup) மற்றும் நீர்வழங்கல் (water‑supply) திட்டம் சேர்த்தால், அரசு கூடுதல் ஊக்கங்கள் (subsidy) வழங்கும்.  
- ஒவ்வொரு திட்டத்தின் **அதிகபட்ச நிதி உதவி, விண்ணப்ப காலம், தேவையான ஆவணங்கள்** ஆகியவை மாநில விவசாயத் துறையின் அதிகாரப்பூர்வ வலைத்தளத்தில் அல்லது NABARD‑இன் “Cold‑Storage Scheme” பக்கத்தில் காணலாம்.  

இப்படிப் பின்பற்றினால், உருளைக்கிழங்கு விலை உயர்ந்தபோது FPO‑வின் மூலம் குளிர்பதன வசதி, பாதுகாப்பான விநியோகம், மற்றும் e‑NAM‑ல் உயர்ந்த விலை பெறும் வாய்ப்பு கிடைக்கும். வாழ்த்துகள்!

నమస్కారం అండి, సాయిల్ టెస్ట్ రిపోర్ట్ లో నత్రజని (N) 120 kg/acre ఉంది. అరటి చెట్లకు వేసుకోవచ్చా లేక తగ్గించాలా?

నమస్కారం అండి! 

మీ సాయిల్ టెస్ట్ రిపోర్ట్ లో నత్రజని (N) **120 kg/acre** ఉంది. ఇది చాలా ఎక్కువ (High) మోతాదు. సాధారణంగా అరటి (Banana) తోటలకు ఎకరాకు సిఫారసు చేసే మొత్తం నత్రజనిలో ఇది సగానికి పైగా లేదా సరిపోయేంత ఉంటుంది. కాబట్టి ఇప్పుడు మీరు **నత్రజని ఎరువులను (యూరియా వంటివి) పూర్తిగా తగ్గించాలి లేదా వేయకూడదు**. 

భూమిలో నత్రజని ఎక్కువైతే ఏమవుతుంది?
* మొక్కల పెరుగుదల విపరీతంగా పెరిగి, కాండం బలహీనపడుతుంది.
* పురుగులు మరియు తెగుళ్లు (ముఖ్యంగా రసం పీల్చే పురుగులు, ఆకు మచ్చలు) ఆశించే అవకాశం పెరుగుతుంది.
* దిగుబడి తగ్గిపోయి, కాయ నాణ్యత దెబ్బతింటుంది.

**మీరు చేయవలసినది:**
1. ప్రస్తుతానికి యూరియా వేయడం పూర్తిగా ఆపండి.
2. భాస్వరం (P), పొటాషియం (K) మరియు పోషకాల వివరాలు కూడా రిపోర్ట్ లో ఉంటే తెలపండి, తద్వారా దానికి తగినట్లుగా పూర్తి ఎరువుల మోతాదును సూచించగలను. 
3. మీ దగ్గర Soil Health Card ఉంటే, అందులోని మిగతా వివరాలు కూడా చూడండి.

নমস্কার! টমেটো‑তে ইউরিয়া (N) ডোজ সোইল হেলথ কার্ডের N‑মানের ওপর নির্ভর করে।  
আপনার **N, P, K মান (kg / ha)** এবং **ক্ষেতের আয়তন (acre/হেক্টর)** দিয়ে আমি সঠিক ডোজ গণনা করতে পারবো।

**দয়া করে জানান:**  

- সোইল হেলথ কার্ডে N (নাইট্রোজেন) মান কত?  
- P (ফসফরাস) এবং K (পটাশ) মানও জানালে ভাল হবে (kg / ha)।  
- আপনার খেতের আয়তন (acre বা hectare) কত?  

এগুলো পেলে `recommend_fertilizer` টুল ব্যবহার করে টমেটো‑এর সর্বোত্তম ইউরিয়া ডোজ (বেসাল + সাইড ড্রেসিং) দেওয়া যাবে, এবং ৫০ কেজি ব্যাগে কত প্যাকেট প্রয়োজন ও জানাব।  

আপনার তথ্য পাঠিয়ে দিন, আমি সঙ্গে সঙ্গেই সুনির্দিষ্ট পরামর্শ দেব। 🙏

**ఉల్లి (ఆనియన్) వేగవంతమైన వృద్ధికి ముఖ్యమైన పోషకాలు**

- **బేసల్ (లవలవాట) పోషకాలు**  
  - N‑P‑K : **100 : 50 : 50 kg / హె.**  
  - 1 ha ≈ 2.5 acre ⇒ **ప్రతి ఎకరుకు**  
    - N ≈ 40 kg (ఉరియా 46 % N)  
    - P₂O₅ ≈ 20 kg (DAP 46 % P₂O₅)  
    - K₂O ≈ 20 kg (MOP 60 % K₂O)  

- **స్ప్లిట్ అప్లికేషన్**  
  1. **బేసల్** – నాటినప్పుడు N ½ (≈ 20 kg), మొత్తం P + K (≈ 20 kg + 20 kg)  
  2. **30 రోజుల తర్వాత** – మిగిలిన N ¼ (≈ 10 kg)  
  3. **60 రోజుల తర్వాత** – చివరి N ¼ (≈ 10 kg)  

- **ఆర్గానిక్ సహాయం**  
  - ఫార్మ్ యార్డ్ మాన్యూర్ (FYM) + వెర్మికాంపోస్ట్ 10‑15 టన్ను / acre, బేసల్‌లో కలపండి.  
  - ఇది మట్టిలో జీవక్రియను పెంచి, రసాయనిక ఎరువుల అవసరాన్ని 10‑15 % తగ్గిస్తుంది.

- **ఉత్పత్తి సూచనలు (క్రయించడానికి లింక్)**  
  - **NPK 10‑26‑26 (50 kg బాగ్)** – బేసల్‌లో P + K + అంత భాగ N కోసం.  
    [/marketplace/product/npk-10-26-26-complex-50kg]  
  - **NPK 20‑20‑0 (50 kg బాగ్)** – N + P బేసల్‌లో (ఉరియా లేకుండా).  
    [/marketplace/product/npk-20-20-0-13-complex-50kg]  

- **పశువులకు ప్రమాదం?**  
  - ఉల్లి వేర్లు, ఆకులు పశువులు ఎక్కువగా తినవు; ప్రధానంగా మానవ వినియోగం.  
  - **రసాయనిక ఎరువులు** (ఉరియా, DAP, MOP) పశువులకు **టాక్సిక్ కాదు**; సరైన మోతాదులో వాడితే మట్టి ద్వారా సురక్షితంగా ఉంటుంది.  
  - **పెస్టిసైడ్లు** (కీటకనాశకాలు) మాత్రమే పశువులకి హానికరంగా ఉండవచ్చు; IPM/ఆర్గానిక్ ఎంపికలు (లవల, నిమ్మ పూత) మొదట ప్రయత్నించండి.

- **సురక్షిత వినియోగ సూచనలు**  
  - ఎరువుల మోతాదు మట్టిలోని NPK విలువల (SHC) ఆధారంగా సర్దుబాటు చేయండి.  
  - వర్షం తర్వాత 24 గంటలలో అప్లై చేయండి, తద్వారా లీకేజ్ తగ్గుతుంది.  
  - ఎరువులపై **ప్రీ‑హార్వెస్ట్ ఇంటర్వెల్** అవసరం లేదు, కానీ కీటకనాశకాలు వాడితే ప్యాకేజ్లో సూచించిన రోజులు (సాధారణంగా 30 రోజులు) పాటించండి.

**సారాంశం:** బేసల్‌లో 40 kg N + 20 kg P₂O₅ + 20 kg K₂O (ప్రతి acre) + 10‑15 t FYM, 3‑స్ప్లిట్ N అప్లికేషన్. పై ఉత్పత్తులు మీ మార్కెట్‌లో లభ్యమవుతాయి; అవసరమైతే మట్టి పరీక్ష (SHC) తీసుకుని మోతాదును సరిచేసుకోవచ్చు.

Bhaiya, kharbuja ki fasal ke sath koun si ghas ya chara ugae ki duno fhayda de?

Bhaiya, Kharbuja ke saath aisi ghas‑charas lagao jo paani, nutrients aur aapke pashuon ke liye dono faydemand ho. Do acche options:

**1. Bajra (Pearl Millet) – Dual‑purpose grain‑fodder**  
- **Kheti ka tarika:** Kharbuja ke rows (≈2 m apart) ke beech 60‑70 cm‑ka interval mein bajra ke beej 2‑3 weeks baad, 15‑20 kg/ha ki matra se sow karo.  
- **Fayde:**  
  - Early growth se mitti ki nmi (N) ko rokta hai, paani ko conserve karta hai.  
  - Kharbuja ke phal ke baad bajra ko cut‑and‑carry ya hay bana ke pashuon ko feed kar sakte ho.  
  - Grain bhi bech kar extra aamdani hoti hai.  

**2. Jowar (Sorghum) – High‑biomass fodder**  
- **Kheti ka tarika:** Kharbuja ke rows ke beech 45‑50 cm spacing par, 12‑15 kg/ha beej daalo, jab Kharbuja ka transplant ho jaye.  
- **Fayde:**  
  - Tez growth, 3‑4 kg dry matter per m² tak, cattle‑feed ke liye best.  
  - Deep root system se soil moisture ko deep tak le jaata hai, isse Kharbuja ko drought stress kam hota hai.  
  - Harvest jowar ko 60‑70 days pe cut karo, phir Kharbuja ko full fruiting tak chhodo.  

**Common tips for dono:**

- **Irrigation:** Same drip/ sprinkler system use karo; ghas ko 1‑2 weeks pehle ya baad paani de, taaki Kharbuja ko paani ki kami na ho.  
- **Fertiliser:** Soil test ke hisaab se 20‑30 kg N/ha extra bajra/jowar ke liye daalo (Kharbuja ko kam N chahiye, isliye balanced).  
- **Harvest timing:** Ghas ko Kharbuja ke fruit set se pehle (30‑40 days) cut karo, taaki competition kam ho.  

**Insurance:** Dono crops ko **PMFBY** ke under insure kar sakte ho – ek hi policy mein multi‑crop cover mil jata hai.  

Agar seed ya fertilizer ka exact price chahiye ho, batao, main marketplace se link bhej dunga. Happy farming!

नमस्ते साहब, मेरे पास धान-कनक वाली ज़मीन है, उसमे आम का पौधा लगाना है। दशहरी या चौसा मे से कोन सा बीज/पेड़ लूँ जो जल्दी फल दे?

नमस्ते! धान-कनक (चिकनी/धान वाली) ज़मीन में आम का पौधा लगाना एक अच्छा विचार है, बशर्ते पानी की सही निकासी का प्रबंध हो क्योंकि आम जलभराव को सहन नहीं कर पाता। 

दशहरी और चौसा में से **दशहरी** किस्म आपके लिए बेहतर रहेगी, क्योंकि:
* **जल्दी फल:** दशहरी जून के शुरुआत में ही पक जाती है, जबकि चौसा जुलाई-अगस्त तक लेट हो जाती है।
* **फलन:** दशहरी में नियमित रूप से (हर साल) या बेहतर मात्रा में फल आते हैं, जबकि चौसा में एकांतर फलन (एक साल छोड़कर) की समस्या अधिक होती है।

**जरूरी बातें:**
* **पौधा चयन:** हमेशा ग्राफ्टेड (कलमी) पौधा ही नर्सरी से लें, बीज से उगाया गया पौधा बहुत देरी से (6-8 साल बाद) फल देता है जबकि कलमी पौधा 3-4 साल में फल देने लगता है।
* **मिट्टी की तैयारी:** धान की ज़मीन में जल निकासी का ध्यान रखें। गड्ढा खोदकर उसमें गोबर की सड़ी खाद, मिट्टी और रेत मिलाकर पौधा लगाएं ताकि जड़ें सड़ें नहीं।

क्या आपको आम के पौधे के खाद या कीट प्रबंधन के बारे में कोई जानकारी चाहिए?

అన్నయ్యా, టమోటా ఆకులు ముడుచుకుపోతున్నాయి, తెల్లగా మచ్చలు పడుతున్నాయి, ఏమి మందు కొట్టాలి?

అన్నయ్యా, టమోటా ఆకులు ముడుచుకుపోవడం మరియు తెల్లగా మచ్చలు పడటం అనేది సాధారణంగా **తెల్ల దోమ (Whiteflies)** లేదా **తామర పురుగులు (Thrips)** ఆశించడం వల్ల, అలాగే కొన్నిసార్లు **లీఫ్ కర్ల్ వైరస్ (Leaf Curl Virus)** వల్ల జరుగుతుంది.

దీని నివారణకు ఈ క్రింది చర్యలు తీసుకోండి:

* **సేంద్రీయ / IPM పద్ధతి:** 
  * నీటిలో కరిగే వేప నూనె (Neem Oil 10000 ppm) 5 మి.లీ లీటరు నీటి కలుపుకుని పిచికారీ చేయండి.
  * పురుగుల ఉధృతిని గమనించడానికి ఎర బుట్టలు (Yellow/Blue Sticky Traps) ఎకరానికి 5-10 ఏర్పాటు చేయండి.
* **రసాయన మందు:**
  * పురుగులు ఎక్కువగా ఉంటే **ఇమిడాక్లోప్రిడ్ (Imidacloprid 17.8% SL)** 0.3 మి.లీ లేదా **థియోమెథాక్స్మ్ (Thiamethoxam 25% WG)** 0.5 గ్రాములు లీటరు నీటికి కలిపి పిచికారీ చేయండి.
  * పిచికారీ చేసేటప్పుడు చేతికి గ్లోవ్స్, ముఖానికి మాస్క్ ధరించండి.

మందులు లేదా స్టికీ ట్రాప్స్ కొనుగోలు చేయడానికి మా [మార్కెట్‌ప్లేస్](/marketplace/product/neem-oil) ని చూడండి.

मंसूर की फसल मऊ में बारिश से डूब गई थी, उसका बीमा क्लेम कैसे मिलेगा?

मऊ में मसूर की फसल में बारिश और जलभराव से हुए नुकसान का बीमा क्लेम (PMFBY के तहत) लेने के लिए नीचे दिए गए कदमों का पालन करें:

* **सूचना दें (72 घंटे के भीतर):** नुकसान होने के 72 घंटे के भीतर बीमा कंपनी, बैंक (जहां से बीमा हुआ है), कृषि विभाग या टोल-फ्री नंबर पर लिखित में सूचना दें। आप 'Crop Insurance' ऐप का भी उपयोग कर सकते हैं।
* **आवश्यक दस्तावेज:**
  * आवेदन पत्र (क्लेम फॉर्म)
  * भूमि के कागजात (खसरा-खतौनी)
  * बैंक पासबुक की फोटोकॉपी
  * आधार कार्ड
  * फसल बुवाई का प्रमाण / स्व-घोषणा पत्र
* **सर्वेक्षण और मुआवजा:** बीमा कंपनी के अधिकारी नुकसान का आकलन करने खेत पर आएंगे। रिपोर्ट सही पाए जाने पर निर्धारित मुआवजा आपके बैंक खाते में भेज दिया जाएगा।

अधिक जानकारी या शिकायत के लिए जिला कृषि अधिकारी कार्यालय या PMFBY की हेल्पलाइन (14447) पर संपर्क करें।

ఉల్లి పంటను పశువులు తింటాయా సార్? దీని వల్ల పాలకు ఏమైనా వాసన వస్తదా అని మా ఊర్లో అడుగుతున్నారు.

ఉల్లి (వెంకాయ) పశువులకు **తినివ్వకూడదు**.  

- **విషపరమైన అంశం** – ఉల్లిలో *అల్లిన్* మరియు *సల్ఫురిక్ యాసిడ్స్* ఉంటాయి. ఇవి పెద్ద పరిమాణంలో తీసుకుంటే పశువుల జీర్ణ వ్యవస్థను గందరగోళానికి దారి తీస్తాయి, కొన్నిసార్లు మలబద్దకం, కోలెస్ట్రాల్ మార్పు, ఇంకా మోతాదు ఎక్కువైతే టాక్సిక్‌ లాగా పనిచేస్తాయి.  

- **పాలు మీద ప్రభావం** – ఉల్లిలోని సల్ఫర్‑ఆధారిత వాసనల (ఉదాహరణకు, “వెల్లి” లేదా “కందిపప్పు” వాసన) పశువుల పళ్లులోకి వెళ్లి, పాలు, పెదవిరి, పాలపదార్థాలు (దూదీ, పెరుగు) లో కూడా అసహజ వాసన లేదా రుచి కలిగించవచ్చు.  

**సిఫార్సు**  
- పశువులకు ఉల్లిని **ఆహారంగా** లేదా **ఖాద్య పదార్థంగా** ఇవ్వకండి.  
- పంట మిగిలిన మిగులు (ఉల్లిపాయ మిగులు, పచ్చి తొక్కలు) పశుపోషకంగా ఉపయోగించాలనుకుంటే, **సాధారణంగా 5 % కు మించి** ఇవ్వకండి, అలాగే **మొదట చిన్న పరిమాణంలో పరీక్ష** చేసి, ఏవైనా అసౌకర్య సూచనలు (అలర్జీ, జీర్ణ సమస్య) కనిపిస్తే వెంటనే ఆపండి.  

**వేరే ఎంపికలు**  
- మిగిలిన పంట మిగులు పశువులకు **వెజిటబుల్ బాయిల్డ్ ఫిడ్స్** లేదా **జన్యు‑సబ్స్టిట్యూట్** (ఉదాహరణకు, మొక్కజొన్న గింజలు, సోయా) ద్వారా పోషకాలు అందించండి.  

ఇలా చేస్తే మీ పశువుల ఆరోగ్యము, పాలు నాణ్యత రెండింటి పరిరక్షణ కూడా ఉంటుంది.

Sahab, mera 2 acre me groundnut ki fasal hai, pani kab kab lagana chahiye yeh batao.

Namaste Sahab! 2 acre groundnut (moongphali) ki fasal ke liye irrigation (pani) ka schedule bahut zaroori hai, khaaskar critical stages par. Groundnut ko lagbhag 4 se 6 paani ki zaroorat padti hai agar barish na ho. 

### Groundnut Irrigation Schedule (Paani Lagane ka Samay):

* **Sowing ke baad (Germination):** Pehla paani sowing ke turant baad dein agar mitti me nami (moisture) kam ho, taki germination achhi ho.
* **Branching Stage (30-35 din par):** Is samay paani dena zaroori hai taki paudhe ki shakhayein achhi banein.
* **Flowering Stage (45-50 din par):** Phool aane ke samay paani ki kami bilkul nahi honi chahiye, warna yield kam ho sakti hai.
* **Pegging Stage (55-65 din par):** Yeh sabse critical stage hai jab phool se sote (pegs) mitti me ghuste hain aur moongphali banti hai. Mitti me nami honi chahiye taki pegs aasani se mitti me ja sakein.
* **Pod Development (70-90 din par):** Dane bharne ke samay niyamit antral par paani dete rahein.
* **Harvesting se 15-20 din pehle:** Katayi (harvesting) se lagbhag 2-3 hafte pehle paani dena band kar dein, taki mitti sukhi ho aur khudaai aasaani se ho sake.

Agar aapke paas Soil Health Card hai ya NPK values pata hain, toh aap bata sakte hain taki hum fertilizer (khaad) ki sahi dose bhi bata sakein.

సార్, మా పెసర, మినప చేనులో ఆకులు ముడుచుకుపోతున్నాయి, మందు కొట్టాలా?

సార్, పెసర మరియు మినప (సజ్జ/ఉద్దు) పంటలలో ఆకులు ముడుచుకుపోవడానికి **తామర పురుగులు (Thrips)**, **తెల్ల దోమ (Whitefly)** లేదా **మొזాయిక్ వైరస్ (Yellow Mosaic Virus)** కారణం కావచ్చు.

దీని నివారణకు ఈ క్రింది చర్యలు తీసుకోండి:

* **సస్యరక్షణ (మందులు):**
  * తామర పురుగులు లేదా తెల్ల దోమ నివారణకు **ఫిప్రోనిల్ 5% SC** (2 మి.లీ. ఒక లీటరు నీటికి కలిపి) లేదా **డైమిథోಯೇಟ್ 30% EC** (2 మి.లీ. ఒక లీటరు నీటికి) పిచికారీ చేయండి.
  * వైరస్ సోకిన ముడత ఆకుల మొక్కలను వేర్లతో సహా పీకి నాశనం చేయండి, ఎందుకంటే ఇది వైరస్ ద్వారా వ్యాపిస్తుంది.
* **జాగ్రత్తలు:**
  * మందు పిచికారీ చేసేటప్పుడు చేతి తొడుగులు, ముఖానికి మాస్క్ ధరించండి. 
  * పురుగుమందుల కొనుగోలుకు మన [మార్కెట్‌ప్లేస్](https://krishidisha.com/marketplace) చూడవచ్చు.

మరింత కచ్చితమైన సలహా కోసం మీ చేనులో తెగులు లక్షణాలు (ఆకుల రంగు, మచ్చలు) ఎలా ఉన్నాయో కొద్దిగా తెలపండి.

माती अहवालात ऑरगॅनिक कार्बन ०.४ टक्केच आहे, नारळाचं उत्पादन वाढवण्यासाठी शेणखत किती टाकावं?

नारळाच्या झाडासाठी मातीतील ०.४% ऑरगॅनिक कार्बन कमी आहे (आदर्श प्रमाण ०.५ ते ०.७५% असते). उत्पादन वाढवण्यासाठी शेणखत आणि सेंद्रिय खतांचा वापर अतिशय महत्त्वाचा आहे.

प्रमाण आणि वेळापत्रक (प्रति झाड वार्षिक):

* **कुजलेले शेणखत किंवा कंपोस्ट:** प्रति झाड **५० किलो** (सुमारे २ ते ३ घमेले) दरवर्षी द्यावे.
* **नारळ शेंड्याचा भुसा (Coir Pith) किंवा गांडूळ खत:** ५ ते १० किलो गांडूळ खत दिल्यास मातीची सुपीकता वेगाने सुधारते.
* **कधी टाकावे:** पावसाळ्याच्या सुरुवातीला (जून-जुलै) किंवा पाऊस ओसरल्यानंतर (सप्टेंबर-ऑक्टोबर) ओल्या मातीत खत द्यावे.

**वाढीव टिप्स:**
* झाडाच्या खोडाभोवती ३ ते ४ फूट गोल आळे करून खत मातीत मिसळावे.
* मातीत ओलावा टिकवण्यासाठी नारळाच्या पाټ्या किंवा शेतातला पालापाचोळा आळ्यामध्ये आच्छादन (Mulching) म्हणून वापरावा. 
* जमिनीची ताकद आणखी वाढवण्यासाठी तागाची हिरवळीची खते (Green Manuring) करून जमिनीत गाडावीत.

சார், உருளைக்கிழங்குக்கு நல்ல விலை கிடைக்க இந்த FPO வழியா நேரடியாக வெளிமாநிலத்துக்கு வியாபாரம் செய்யலாமா?

வணக்கம்! FPO (உற்பப்பாளர் நிறுவனம்) மூலமாக உருளைக்கிழங்கை வெளிமாநிலங்களுக்கு நேரடியாக வியாபாரம் செய்வது நல்ல லாபம் தரும் ஒரு சிறந்த முடிவு.

FPO மூலம் நீங்கள் என்னென்ன நன்மைகளைப் பெறலாம்:
- **மொத்த விற்பனை:** சிறு விவசாயிகளை ஒருங்கிணைத்து பெரிய அளவில் விற்கும்போது போக்குவரத்து செலவு குறையும்.
- **மத்திய அரசின் FPO திட்டம்:** 10,000 புதிய FPO-க்களை உருவாக்கும் மத்திய அரசின் திட்டத்தின் கீழ், FPO-க்களுக்கு நிதி மற்றும் சந்தை வாய்ப்புகள் கிடைக்கின்றன.
- **மண்டிகளை இணைக்கும் e-NAM:** நாடு முழுவதும் உள்ள 1,400-க்கும் மேற்பட்ட APMC மண்டிகளை இணைக்கும் **e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)** இணையதளத்தைப் பயன்படுத்தி வெளிமாநில வர்த்தகர்களை ஆன்லைன் மூலம் தொடர்பு கொள்ளலாம்.
- **கிசான் ரெயில் (Kisan Rail):** உருளைக்கிழங்கு போன்ற அழுகும் பொருட்களை விரைவாகவும், குறைந்த கட்டணத்திலும் குளிர்சாதன வசதியுடன் வெளிமாநிலச் சந்தைகளுக்கு அனுப்ப கிசான் ரெயில் சேவையைப் பயன்படுத்தலாம்.

**முக்கிய குறிப்பு:** வெளிமாநிலம் அனுப்பும் முன், அந்த மாநிலத்தில் உருளைக்கிழங்குக்கான தற்போதைய சந்தை விலை (Mandi Price) மற்றும் தரக்கட்டுப்பாடுகளை சரிபார்த்துக் கொள்வது நல்லது.

Sir, mere khet me N 140, P 22, K 280 aur pH 7.8 hai, isme dhan ki kitni pedaavar aa jayegi?

Aapke soil test values (N 140, P 22, K 280, pH 7.8) acche hain, lekin **pH 7.8 thoda alkaline hai** – dhan (rice) ke liye ideal pH 5.5–6.5 hota hai. Yield estimate ke liye mujhe kuch aur details chahiye:

1. **State** (kaunse state mein khet hai?)  
2. **Area** (kitne hectare/acre?)  
3. **Annual rainfall** (mm mein, ya nearest town ka naam)  
4. **Crop year** (kaunsa saal – 2024, 2025?)  
5. **Season** – Kharif hi na? (Rabi/Boro bhi ho sakta hai)

Ye details dein, main **predict_yield** tool se point estimate, expected range aur baseline yield nikaal dunga.
